title: Does Private Country-by-Country Reporting Deter Tax Avoidance & Income Shifting? Evidence from BEPS Action Item 13

scopes.description: Full supplied Stata workflow: primary tax-avoidance preparation/tests (Tables 4–7) and the separately dependent affiliate/parent income-shifting preparation/tests (Table 8). The code file is the exact entry point, but the required data loaders, generated handoffs and some field producers are absent. Appendix-only results without a supplied branch are contextual.

requirements.description: BvD identifier lookup supplied for Orbis firm selection/validation. The streamed text contains a header and 18,619 nonblank identifier entries; uniqueness and identifier-to-panel match completeness were not tested. This list is not an analysis panel.

requirements.description: Orbis annual financial-statement and ownership panel for EU-headquartered global ultimate owners with foreign subsidiaries, excluding financial and extractive firms; author states 2010–2018 and 5,312 firms/57,131 firm-year ends. The supplied code reshapes this input using the literal varlist stub, then expects BvDIDnumber, Year, country, ISIN, Conscode, Revenue, HQLocatedEU, TaxationmEUR, PLbeforetaxmEUR, PTI, TA, NetIncome, Totalassets, TotalEquityLiab, ShareholdersfundsmEUR, Intangibles, RD, Numberofpatents and Numberoftrademarks. The source wide-column names/pattern that satisfy varlist are unknown. It sets PYRevenue to the previous available Revenue row by BvDIDnumber; if 2010 rows are intended in the Table 5 pre-period, their prior row would require 2009 data. Calendar-gap, duplicate-year and first-year rules remain unspecified.

requirements.description: Country-Year OECD statutory tax-rate series used directly as STR, merged into the primary panel by country and Year and used in TaxDiff and affiliate-group C construction. issues.description: The only Stata file does not load the primary data and directly references STR Only.dta and CETR.dta at machine-specific Windows paths. The income-shifting branch separately references ParentData.dta and a reshaped affiliate input; the file later returns to primary-panel Table 7 outcomes after the Table 8 affiliate branch without restoring that dataset. It creates POST in both branches, but no clear/load/driver transition establishes separate datasets or run order. Exact producers, current directories and host-visible relative paths must be supplied; do not infer a single-session workflow.

The raw Compustat-to-CETR.dta producer is absent. Code later expects CashTaxes_CETR_w, PTI_CETR_w and TA_CETR, but no source-column mapping, fiscal-year conversion, currency/unit transformation, winsorization population/rule, or output producer is supplied. The catalog-listed global Funda candidate and one-row read do not establish complete match coverage.

Step 6 says discrepant Orbis/Compustat observations are excluded, but the supplied code only generates Match and Match1 equality flags and does not filter on them. The intended discrepancy rule, units/tolerance and whether these flags drive deletion remain unresolved.

The income-shifting code documents C as a weighted average of affiliates’ statutory rates but supplies no C producer or complete implementation contract. It creates POST_CBCR, C_POST and C_POST_CBCR, while regressions reference CBCR_POST, C_CBCR and C_CBCR_POST; it creates perctmissing but filters on perctmissingC. Do not guess replacements or supply a proxy variable.

Both primary and income-shifting sections reshape an unprovided wide panel using the literal varlist stub and BvDIDnumber key. The affiliate branch additionally expects parent GUOBvDIDnumber and annual fields. No source column schema, producer, key uniqueness, or relationship between the affiliate input and ParentData.dta is supplied.
Table 4 requires BW1_250, BW1_450 and BW1_550, but the code never creates or imports them and the package does not document their eligibility rules.

The Stata source calls misisng() on four lines (34, 53, 58 and 208) and uses a single equals sign in the HQLocatedEU=1 condition on line 144. These are supported spelling/operator corrections; exact line edits are included.
The raw narrative heading Calculation of C is not a Stata comment and will be parsed as a command. A comment marker is an unambiguous supported correction; it does not supply the missing C producer.

The source writes gen R&D=..., using an ampersand in a Stata variable name. The formula uses RD divided by assets, but the intended valid variable name/alias is not established; preserve this block and ask for the target name rather than invent one.

The code generates CETR, MissingCETR, CETR_R and CETR_T from CashTaxPaid/PLbeforetaxmEUR, then generates the same names again using CashTaxes_CETR_w/PTI_CETR_w. Stata cannot execute both gen blocks in one data state. The first block also assigns CETR_T from ETR. Which source variant is intended and how both documented variants should be retained is unresolved. Do not silently select, delete or overwrite a source variant.

The PYRevenue statement calls egen with a bare expression, not an egen function, and uses _n-1 within firm rows. The executable construction and whether PYRevenue means the previous observation or previous calendar year (including missing/duplicate year handling and the first required observation) are unresolved.
The source uses rename MaxCBCR CBCR if Equals==1. Stata rename does not act on observations through an if qualifier; the intended condition-specific variable disposition cannot be inferred safely.

Lines 19–28 are explanatory primary-sample prose embedded in the .do file without comment markers, so Stata parses them as commands. The block is unambiguously documentation; comment-only prefixing preserves the text and executable commands.

edits.before:
The primary sample in the study consists of EU MNCs. I restrict the sample to EU MNCs because CbCr was effective in EU member states on the same date (January 1, 2016). 
In addition, the tax and legal environments in EU nations are comparable across jurisdictions, and there is better availability of affiliate-level data through 
databases compiled by Bureau van Dijk. I obtain annual financial statements and ownership data for the years 2010 to 2018 from the Orbis database (Bureau van Dijk). 
In the EU, a primary reporting obligation under CbCr arises when, in a multinational group, either the ultimate parent or a member of the group is resident in 
a member state. CbCr requirements for resident and nonresident EU firms when the parent entity is headquartered outside an EU member state depends on whether 
the parent jurisdiction has adopted the rules and on the exchange relationship between parent home country and EU member states. I therefore restrict my primary 
sample to EU headquartered firms and, in an additional analysis (section 8.3), include nonresident EU firms. I start with EU-headquartered firms that are identified 
as global ultimate owners in the Orbis database and that have at least one foreign subsidiary. I exclude financial institutions and firms in the extractive industries 
because they are subject to additional CbCr requirements.  After excluding firms with missing data required to calculate the regression variables, the final sample
 consists of 5,312 EU-headquartered multinationals (57,131 firm year-ends).
